templates.label: Accordion
templates.notes: Native details/summary disclosure with an accessible editorial row.

templates.label: Pullquote
templates.notes: A short, evidence-backed rhetorical pause. Thesis and editorial-note treatments are variants of the same bounded block.

templates.label: Margin note
templates.notes: Short attributed aside with a rust marker.

templates.label: Editorial table
templates.notes: Semantic, div-based tabular rows; needs a strict table schema before Studio output.

templates.label: Code card
templates.notes: Structured code/schema panel; must remain plain text and never accept arbitrary markup.

templates.label: Chip / code-token row
templates.notes: Named fields, evidence attributes, and gate lists; requires a bounded item schema.

templates.label: Annotated artifact
templates.notes: A primary record, package, or run shown with bounded callouts. The artifact and every annotation must come from supplied evidence.

templates.label: Comparison matrix
templates.notes: A numbered table comparing named rows across a fixed set of subjects, each column marked by a categorical tone. Cells take a small span AST (plain, strong, code, status), never markup; a missing cell renders UNKNOWN. Narrow screens stack each row and every cell names its subject.

templates.label: Equivalence matrix
templates.notes: Named equivalents for one capability across a fixed set of subjects. Each cell is a structured entity (name, source link, lifecycle status, note), never markup; a nameless entity renders as no offering and a missing cell renders UNKNOWN. Lifecycle statuses come from a bounded set, and flags that mean plan a migration draw in rust. A row can carry an always-visible editor’s note. The host supplies the filter text and emphasised subject, so one control can drive every matrix in an essay.

templates.label: Subject profiles
templates.notes: Side-by-side fact columns, one per subject, each marked by a categorical tone: an optional headline figure, a fact sheet, points, labelled notes, and a closing verdict. The figure is a supplied string displayed as written; it is never scaled, charted, or ranked across columns. One column on narrow screens.

templates.label: System flow
templates.notes: A reusable, typed system schematic with configurable components, path roles, freeform layout, and restrained motion. A host can follow the active step to show authored detail beside the figure. It remains a Studio candidate until its configuration has a runtime schema and renderer contract.

templates.label: Sequence flow
templates.notes: An ordered handoff among typed stages. Provenance is one evidence-bound variant, not the primitive name.

templates.label: Feedback loop
templates.notes: Nested and learning loops prove the pattern, but the current figures are bespoke.

templates.label: Layered stack
templates.notes: The primitive's isometric-callouts variant (the four-disciplines infographic) is an enabled, typed visual plan. This entry stays a candidate so the generic manual stack template remains on the canvas; Plane stack and AI X-Ray remain fixtures for the vertical and crosscutting-spine treatments.

templates.label: Architecture stack
templates.notes: A conceptual reference architecture read top to bottom: supplied tiers (primary, plain, or external) with chips, cells, and side-by-side splits, joined by labelled connectors. Several stacks in one row compare architectures. It is conceptual, not a deployment diagram, and distinct from the isometric layered-stack infographic.

templates.label: Pipeline / flow
templates.notes: Cycle, compiler, IR stages, and coordination chain are related but need separate bounded variants.

templates.label: Branching tree
templates.notes: The coordination router proves the need; a safe tree data renderer is still absent.

templates.label: Node-edge network
templates.notes: System topology and peer mesh must preserve roles, permissions, and sparse topology.

templates.label: Crosswalk
templates.notes: Three-column requirements-to-control-to-test mapping; absent from the original sample list but a real FieldNotes pattern.

templates.label: Funnel
templates.notes: Tapered convergence or decision stages; labels and outcomes must remain explicit.

templates.label: Bus
templates.notes: A shared spine connecting one capability to several consumers or processes.

templates.label: Translation bridge
templates.notes: A bridge that maps concepts between two systems through an explicit intermediate representation.

templates.label: Continuum
templates.notes: An ordered range with named endpoints, positions, and explicit indeterminate states.

templates.label: State track
templates.notes: Ordered states and gates for a lifecycle; distinct from a historical timeline.

templates.label: Orbital system
templates.notes: A central reference state surrounded by related actors, cases, or outcomes.

templates.label: Comparison
templates.notes: Matched structures shown side by side so differences, tradeoffs, or migration can be inspected.

templates.label: Semantic matrix
templates.notes: Items positioned against two named semantic dimensions; quantitative frontiers remain data visualizations.

templates.label: Assembly
templates.notes: Parts combine into a bounded whole; used for assertion blocks, factories, and packaged deliverables.

templates.label: Semantic equation
templates.notes: Named concepts related by operators. It explains a model and does not imply numerical calculation.

templates.label: Curve
templates.notes: A qualitative trajectory over an explicitly named progression; scaled quantitative curves belong in the chart catalog.

templates.label: Staircase
templates.notes: Discrete levels shown as steps. Maturity levels ascend; the price-staircase variant descends on a log scale, holds each level until the next release, and draws in once on first view with labels that settle without colliding.

templates.label: Nested containment
templates.notes: Concentric or nested regions that communicate scope, ownership, or reinforcing layers.

templates.label: Swimlane
templates.notes: Events organized by actor or system lane so responsibility and handoffs remain visible.

templates.label: Boundary
templates.notes: A named perimeter that separates authority, responsibility, or allowed action.

templates.label: Region grid
templates.notes: Named regions (pillars, a brief, a SWOT) each holding the points that belong to it. Adapted from Interactive Response grid widgets.

templates.label: Horizons
templates.notes: Ordered columns for horizons or phases. Order is sequence, not magnitude; dated events belong in the timeline.

templates.label: Card grid
templates.notes: Repeated cards with a bounded glyph or monogram, a label, a short annotation, and detail: findings, uncertainties, or people.

avoidWhen: the layers do not build on one another
a conventional chart would communicate the data more directly
the asset has no meaningful sub-parts to address

charts.name: Bar / column
charts.question: Length on a common baseline: the most accurately decoded quantitative encoding.
charts.record: { category: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Grouped bar
charts.question: An inner band scale nests a second category inside each primary category.
charts.record: { category: nominal, series: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Dot plot
charts.question: Every group in a row shares one position scale, so gaps read as precisely as bars. A range rule carries the spread and one reference series anchors the comparison.
charts.record: { category: nominal, series: nominal, value: quantitative | null }

charts.name: Stacked column
charts.question: Composition by stacked lengths. The total shares a baseline; the segments do not.
charts.record: { period: ordinal, segment: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Histogram
charts.question: Continuous values binned into adjacent tiles; bin width is a stated design decision.
charts.record: { value: quantitative } (binned by renderer)

charts.name: Line
charts.question: A path connecting positions. It encodes direction and slope, not magnitude.
charts.record: { period: ordinal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Multi-series line
charts.question: One line per category, distinguished by hue and redundantly by shape.
charts.record: { period: ordinal, series: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Slope chart
charts.question: Two periods connected. Direction is the entire message; everything else is removed.
charts.record: { category: nominal, valueA: quantitative, valueB: quantitative }

charts.name: Area
charts.question: A line with the region beneath filled, emphasizing accumulated magnitude.
charts.record: { period: ordinal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Stacked area
charts.question: Composition over time. Order matters because only the bottom band has a common baseline.
charts.record: { period: ordinal, segment: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Bar + line
charts.question: Aligned layers share x but use separate, explicitly labeled quantitative scales.
charts.record: { period: ordinal, volume: quantitative, rate: quantitative }

charts.name: Scatter plot
charts.question: Two quantitative positions reveal association, outliers, and clusters.
charts.record: { x: quantitative, y: quantitative, group?: nominal }

charts.name: Bubble chart
charts.question: A scatter plot with a third variable mapped to area; outliers must be labeled.
charts.record: { x: quantitative, y: quantitative, size: quantitative, group?: nominal }

charts.name: Heat map
charts.question: A grid of tiles varying by luminance: position carries category, color carries value.
charts.record: { row: nominal, column: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Tile grid map
charts.question: A choropleth-like map that gives every region equal area and stable position.
charts.record: { region: nominal, row: ordinal, col: ordinal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Choropleth map
charts.question: Real geography carries identity and luminance carries value, for every state, county, or congressional district. Area is a side effect, never the message.
charts.record: { region: FIPS | postal code | name, value: quantitative, label?: nominal }

charts.name: Box plot
charts.question: A five-number summary plus outliers, exposing spread and skew hidden by a mean.
charts.record: { group: nominal, values: quantitative[] }

charts.name: Waterfall
charts.question: Cumulative arithmetic made visible; increases and decreases are semantic states.
charts.record: { step: nominal, delta: quantitative }

charts.name: Funnel
charts.question: Ordered stages with monotonically decreasing length. Drop-off is the story.
charts.record: { stage: ordinal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Doughnut
charts.question: Angle is decoded poorly; use few parts and state values directly.
charts.record: { segment: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Tree map
charts.question: Containment plus area shows two hierarchy levels in one rectangle.
charts.record: { group: nominal, name: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Circle packing
charts.question: Literal nesting reveals structure but compares magnitude less precisely than a tree map.
charts.record: { group: nominal, name: nominal, value: quantitative }

charts.name: Sunburst
charts.question: Concentric rings of arcs: angle carries magnitude, radius carries depth, and adjacency carries containment.
charts.record: { id: nominal, label: nominal, parent?: nominal, value?: quantitative }

charts.name: Sankey
charts.question: Nodes are rectangles and conserved ribbon width carries volume from source to target.
charts.record: { nodes: Node[], links: { source, target, value }[] }

charts.name: Chord chart
charts.question: A square adjacency matrix bent into a circle; ribbons show mutual volume.
charts.record: { names: nominal[], matrix: quantitative[][] }

charts.name: Node-link network
charts.question: Connection is primary. Node position carries no value, only topology.
charts.record: { nodes: Node[], links: { source, target, strength }[] }

charts.name: Decision tree
charts.question: Ordered decisions contain terminal outcomes; every leaf is decidable.
charts.record: { name, note?, class?, children?: recursive }

charts.name: Dendrogram
charts.question: Pure structure: depth and adjacency mean something; horizontal order does not.
charts.record: { name, children?: recursive }

presets.label: Decision brief
presets.description: State a position, why it holds, what it changes, and the next move.

presets.label: Claim / evidence matrix
presets.description: Sort claims by how well the sources support them.

presets.label: Assumptions & open questions
presets.description: Make what the argument takes for granted visible.

presets.label: Uncertainties
presets.description: List what is not known, how confident you are, and what would resolve it.

presets.label: Prompt & response
presets.description: Record a prompt and the reply it produced at each thinking level.

presets.label: Concept map
presets.description: Group the parts of a system into named regions.

presets.label: Responsibility swimlane
presets.description: Show who does what, and where work is handed off.

presets.label: Method with gates
presets.description: Ordered stages, each with the check that must pass before moving on.

presets.label: Concept model
presets.description: Define the concepts in play, their properties, and how they relate.

presets.label: Before / after
presets.description: Contrast a current state with a connected future one.

presets.label: Now / next / later
presets.description: Arrange initiatives or ideas across three horizons.

presets.label: Two-by-two
presets.description: Position ideas against two named dimensions.

presets.label: Key findings
presets.description: Lead with the measures and results that carry the argument.

presets.label: People & perspectives
presets.description: Introduce the people whose views shape the story.
